FY26 period: 52 weeks to 28 March 2026; RNS dated 18 June 2026 (CEO letter 17 June 2026) (source: same).

Group adjusted revenue £1,715.7m (+25% vs FY25 £1,370.0m); First Bus £1,443.6m (FY25 £1,081.5m); First Rail adjusted revenue £272.4m (FY25 £288.8m), split DfT TOCs & Rail Services £130.6m and open access/rail contracts £141.8m; group eliminations (£0.3)m (source: same).
First Bus revenue mix: Regional Bus £891.3m, Business & Coach £230.1m, Franchising £322.2m (includes ~£310m First Bus London); statutory First Bus revenue equals adjusted at £1,443.6m (source: same).

Statutory group revenue (continuing) £4,751.9m (FY25 restated £5,233.9m), driven mainly by First Rail gross DfT TOC pass-through £3,327.6m; statutory First Rail revenue fell on SWR transfer to DfTO (source: same).

Group adjusted operating profit (continuing) £219.4m (FY25 £222.8m), marginally lower; excluding DfT TOCs, adjusted operating profit grew 18%; total incl. discontinued £221.5m (FY25 £222.2m) (source: same).

First Bus adjusted operating profit £102.8m (+7% vs FY25 £96.0m); First Rail adjusted operating profit £129.9m (FY25 £148.8m), with open access adjusted OP £25.6m (FY25 £34.1m) after Stirling mobilisation and Lumo infrastructure charge (source: same).
Statutory operating profit (continuing) £219.4m (FY25 £222.6m); statutory total £221.5m (FY25 £227.5m)—matches adjusted in FY26 as no adjusting items (source: same).

Adjusted EPS (continuing) 20.3p (FY25 19.4p); total adjusted EPS 20.7p incl. discontinued 0.4p (FY25 19.3p); basic/statutory EPS 21.4p (FY25 21.3p); weighted average shares 553.4m (FY25 597.7m); shares in issue 542.6m ex-treasury/EBT (source: same).

Cash generated by operations £681.5m (FY25 £828.2m); cash capex (£253.0)m; First Bus net capex £188.2m; highlights cite ~£190m accelerated First Bus electrification capex and ~£35m growth investment/acquisitions (source: same).

Company-defined free cash flow £73.8m (FY25 £113.5m): reconciled from adjusted cash flow (£124.0)m by adding back acquisitions £35.3m, dividends £38.9m and buyback £50.4m—described in highlights as 'before acquisitions and returns' (source: same).

Cash £169.6m; ring-fenced cash £262.4m (First Rail £260.8m, other £1.6m); reported net debt £725.3m (FY25 £985.6m); adjusted net debt £137.7m (FY25 £86.9m)—excludes IFRS 16 leases and ring-fenced cash; pre-IFRS 16 net cash on bonds/bank/other debt (£124.7)m (source: same).

IFRS 16 lease liabilities £850.0m total (rail £702.3m, non-rail £147.7m); DfT TOC IFRS 16 leases on balance sheet £649.2m (FY25 £1,020.4m); net IFRS 16 operating profit impact £45.6m (FY25 £49.4m) (source: same).

Final dividend proposed 5.0p; FY26 total dividend 7.2p (FY25 6.5p), payable ~£27m final on 7 Aug 2026; dividends paid in FY26 £39m (external £38.9m); policy ~3x cover of adjusted earnings, tightening towards 2.5x over time (~2.8x on 20.3p/7.2p); FCF cover vs cash dividends paid ~1.9x (£73.8m/£38.9m) (source: same).

Shareholder returns FY26: ~£89m via dividends and completed £50m buyback; further £100m buyback announced, expected to complete within next 12 months; ~£100m anticipated via buyback over FY27–FY28 (source: same).

Rail transition/nationalisation: SWR to DfTO 25 May 2025; GWR NRC expires 13 Dec 2026 (handover to DfT Operator); WCP transfer expected around end FY27; National Rail Contracts moving to public ownership/GBR; ~£90m cash inflow anticipated over three years from Apr 2026 as GWR/WCP transition (source: same).

Open access: revenue £109.3m, 3.1m journeys (+4%); on course to more than double capacity in 2–3 years; ORR applications for ~1bn annual seat miles under review; Stirling service fully operational from Jul 2026; Carmarthen from Dec 2027 (source: same).

London Overground: contract awarded Dec 2025, mobilised 3 May 2026; eight-year term plus two-year TfL option; ~£300m anticipated revenue in FY27; ~£3bn over contract life; TfL retains revenue risk (source: same).

FY27 outlook: maintain adjusted EPS from higher-quality base; First Bus revenue just over £1.5bn with further adjusted OP progress and ~£140m decarbonisation capex; open access revenue ~£130–150m, margin progressing to mid-teens; Overground ~£300m; lower DfT TOC adjusted revenue; ~£400m FCF anticipated over next three years (source: same).
